key_evidence_spans: She became pale and lost consciousness; bystander ECG showed ventricular fibrillation.
In the intensive care unit, her differential diagnosis included channelopathies, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and metabolic abnormalities.
Initial electrocardiogram revealed sinus rhythm with interpolated premature ventricular complexes and a QTc of 380 ms
Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated an ejection fraction of 45–50%, normal wall thickness, and no valvular abnormalities.
On arrival, her blood pressure was 93/70 mmHg, pulse 86 bpm, and oxygen saturation 100% (bag–valve–mask)
Return of spontaneous circulation was achieved after two defibrillations.
An intravenous amiodarone infusion (1 mg/min) and oral amiodarone 400 mg were administered.
